# 1. Introduction

We track whether QQ Music's seven public toplists -- Hot Songs
(热歌榜), Online Songs (网络歌曲榜), Mainland (内地榜), Rap (说唱榜),
EDM (电音榜), Guofeng (国风热歌榜), and Douyin Hit (抖音热歌榜) --
shifted in a measurable way across 2018-2024. We use only the data
that QQ's public musicu.fcg endpoint exposes with no login: chart
metadata, ranks, week-on-chart counts. **No audio, no transcripts, no
play-counts per song**, because those endpoints now require login
(`code=500003`).

The original proposal listed "2015-2025". After probing the API we
narrow the actual data window to **2018 week 30 - 2024 week 52** (the
`period` parameter is silently clamped outside this range).

```{r load}
song_year_all  <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/song_year_all.csv"),
                            show_col_types = FALSE)

                            show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 2.1 Toplists and coverage

Seven QQ toplists are pulled, each with weekly issues from 2018W30
to 2024W52 (some start later because of topId-specific data
availability):

| topId | Title | Issues | Unique songs | Genre tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 26 | 热歌榜 | 202 | 1942 | - |
| 28 | 网络歌曲榜 | 331 | 9626 | - |
| 5 | 内地榜 | 288 | 10928 | - |
| 58 | 说唱榜 | 195 | 3125 | rap |
| 57 | 电音榜 | 191 | 2878 | edm |
| 65 | 国风热歌榜 | 194 | 1303 | guofeng |
| 60 | 抖音热歌榜 | 167 | 1729 | - |

Total ~137,000 song-week rows after collapsing the long sheet into
`song_year_all`.

```{r coverage}
cov <- raw %>%
  group_by(top_title, year) %>%
  summarise(weeks_recorded = n_distinct(period),
            songs = n_distinct(song_id),
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(head(cov, 12))
```

# 3. Cross-chart correlation

```{r align, out.width="80%"}

```

```{r align_view}
wide_corr <- topid_overview %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Var2, values_from = cor)
knitr::kable(wide_corr, digits = 2,
             caption = "Cross-chart correlation of yearly mean log(1+weeks)")
```

Key reading: **0.92** between Hot Songs (热歌榜) and Online Songs
(网络歌曲榜); **0.72** between Hot Songs and Guofeng (国风热歌榜);
**-0.89** between Hot Songs and Rap (说唱榜). Rap and Douyin Hit
strongly anti-correlate, indicating separate ecosystems.

# 4. Yearly drift (chart-history features only)

We do **not** run PCA / PLS / t-SNE on audio embeddings in this
draft (audio features are out-of-scope per user request). What we
*can* extract from chart metadata alone is the per-year mean of
two simple aggregates:

- `avg_weeks`: mean `weeks_total` per song per year.
- `avg_peak`: mean `peak_rank_min` per song per year.

These are deliberately low-dimensional. They answer the questions
"did songs stay longer on chart?" and "did songs reach better
peaks?". They do **not** answer "did the audio character of songs
drift?" — that would require MERT / librosa features.

```{r yearly_summary}
yearly <- song_year_all %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(song_id),
            avg_weeks = mean(weeks_total, na.rm = TRUE),
            avg_peak  = mean(peak_rank_min, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(year)
knitr::kable(yearly, digits = 2,
             caption = "Yearly chart-history summary (chart-metadata features only, NOT audio features)")
```

```{r yearly_plots, out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/year_avg_weeks.png"))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/year_avg_peak.png"))
```

# 5. Flow summary

```{r flow}
song_year_all_with_flags <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT,
  "data/interim/song_year_all_with_flags.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
flags <- song_year_all_with_flags %>%
  summarise(live = sum(is_live, na.rm = TRUE),
            cover = sum(is_cover, na.rm = TRUE),
            remix = sum(is_remix, na.rm = TRUE),
```


## 7.1 LOF-based outlier detection (alternative)

Euclidean distance from the year-centroid catches songs that are
globally distant. **Local Outlier Factor** catches songs that are
locally atypical within their year — i.e. a song that is not
necessarily far from the year centroid, but is less dense than its
nearest neighbours.

```{r lof}
lof_out <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/year_top5_most_outlier_lof.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lof_out %>% select(year, song_title, singer_name, lof),
             caption = "Most outlier song per year by LOF (Local Outlier Factor)")
```

```{r lof_compare}
lof_compare <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/lof_vs_euclidean_overlap.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lof_compare,
             caption = "LOF-top5 vs Euclidean-top5: how many songs both methods agree on per year")
```

The two methods rarely agree (typically 0-1 of 5 songs per year).
LOF surfaces **short-cycle hits** that briefly reached high rank
and disappeared (e.g. 2018: 叶炫清《说谎的人》peak rank 6 in 1
week). Euclidean surfaces songs that are globally unusual in
shape (e.g. an old classic with high weeks_total but mid-rank).
We report both so the reviewer can pick the definition of
"atypical" that fits their interest.

# 9. Cross-platform validation (timeline + QQ changepoints)

The previous overlap-based check (40.5 % between QQ and NetEase
current snapshot) does **not** validate QQ conclusions: overlap
percentages are dominated by licensing and regional catalogue
differences, not by listener behaviour. We replace it with a
**timeline-based cross-platform check**.

## 9.1 Deep dive: features extracted from QQ data during the COVID-Q1 2020 window

We focus the rest of the report on the 2020 changepoint, because
the QQ data has rich week-by-week resolution there. We compare
four regimes:

| Regime | Definition | Weeks in data |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_covid`     | 2018W30 .. 2019W52              | 73 |
| `covid_q1`      | 2020W04 .. 2020W17 (Wuhan lockdown + nationwide stay-at-home) | 14 |
| `covid_recovery` | 2020W18 .. 2020W26               | 9 |
| `post_covid`    | 2020W27 .. 2020W52              | 26 |

```{r covid_features}
covid <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/covid_period_features.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(covid, digits = 1,
             caption = "QQ chart-history features extracted per regime (from R/15_covid_qq_features.R)")
```

```{r covid_plot, out.width="90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/covid_period_qq_features.png"))
```

**Three observations from QQ data alone**:

1. **During COVID-Q1 2020, both `unique_songs_per_week` and
   `new_songs_per_week` drop to their lowest levels across the
   2018-2024 window** (240 / 61.5 vs the pre-COVID baseline of
   280 / 84.7 and the post-COVID value of 440 / 120). The Chinese
   music industry's new-release pipeline effectively stalled
   during the lockdown.
2. **After the lockdown ends** (recovery phase 2020W18-W26),
   values snap back to the pre-COVID baseline. No structural
   break yet.
3. **The structural break is `post_covid` (2020W27+)** — chart
   volume jumps to 440 unique songs per week and 120 new songs
   per week, **1.5x the pre-COVID level**. The 2020 changepoint
   is therefore best interpreted as "the *post*-lockdown
   acceleration" — the same industry that had been paused during
   the lockdown flooded the platform from mid-2020 onward.

## 9.1.1 Why these features, and not others

We do **not** attempt a more granular sentiment- or genre-level
analysis of the COVID window. Such analysis would require audio
features (MFCC, chroma, etc.) or lyrics — both explicitly
out-of-scope in this draft per user request. What we *can* extract
from chart metadata alone is **release volume** and **chart
churn**, and those two features turn out to be the strongest
COVID-period signals.

## 9.1.2 What this analysis does NOT cover

Three follow-up questions would tighten the QQ-Covid story but
require additional data sources:

1. **Genre mix during COVID-Q1**: did rap/EDM/guofeng respond
   differently to the lockdown? Answerable from our genre-tagged
   charts; would take ~30 minutes more.
2. **QQ platform-specific vs. national**: did NetEase / Kugou
   also drop their per-week unique-song count during 2020-Q1?
   Answerable only if a NetEase historical weekly endpoint
   becomes available; currently not.
3. **Did the post-COVID surge consist mostly of new songs or
   also "rediscovered old songs"?** Answerable from our
   publish-year column on each song: we can classify each
   week's entry as "new release" vs "back-catalog".

## 9.2 Cross-region patterns beyond song-overlap

Song-overlap is dominated by licensing and regional catalogue
differences (Section 9.1 of the cross-platform notebook — `R/17`).
We instead ask **structural** questions on the same snapshots:

1. What fraction of the top-N are songs released in 2018 or earlier
   (the "old catalogue" share)?
2. How concentrated is the top-N among a small number of artists
   (the Gini coefficient on per-artist rank counts)?

These two metrics are **directly related to QQ-derived claims**:

- The QQ chart-history shows **songs released years ago still chart**
  (e.g. 张信哲《过火》1995 in 2018 chart). This is consistent
  with "QQ users are exposed to old catalogue" — but is this a
  Chinese-market pattern, or a QQ-platform artefact?
- QQ's 2022 changepoint splits charts into a Douyin-driven cluster
  and a QQ-algorithm cluster. Does that correspond to a
  star-concentration shift on QQ, or is star-concentration a
  Chinese-market pattern?

```{r cross_region_metrics}
cr <- read_csv(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/cross_region_patterns.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cr, digits = 1,
             caption = "Cross-region structural metrics (R/17)")
```

```{r cross_region_share_old, out.width="80%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/cross_region_share_old.png"))
```

```{r cross_region_artist_gini, out.width="80%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/cross_region_artist_gini.png"))
```

```{r cross_region_top3_share, out.width="80%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(ROOT, "data/interim/cross_region_top3_share.png"))
```

### 9.2.1 What the cross-region snapshot adds to QQ findings

**Three structural findings, none of which QQ's chart-history alone
shows**:

1. **"Old catalogue share" is bimodal between platforms, not
   bimodal between regions.** Apple Music CN has **84 %** of its
   top-50 released 2018 or earlier (Jay Chou, Sun Yanzi, Liang
   Jingru fill the slots). QQ has only **18.9 %**. The two are
   Chinese-language platforms but their catalogue freshness
   differs by 65 percentage points. The QQ chart-history's
   "old songs still chart" observation is therefore a
   **QQ-platform pattern, not a Chinese-market pattern** —
   Apple Music CN does it much more strongly.
2. **Star concentration is highest on Apple Music CN (54 %),
   not on QQ (24.5 %).** This reverses the naive hypothesis
   ("QQ = star-driven platform because 2022 ecosystem split").
   The 2022 QQ-platform split was *between* Douyin-driven and
   QQ-algorithm-driven streams, but **QQ itself is comparatively
   artist-diverse** within its top 200.
3. **NetEase is the most artist-diverse (9.1 % top-3 share)**,
   consistent with NetEase's reputation as the indie /
   singer-songwriter platform. Apple Music US is intermediate
   (38 %); Apple Music CN is most concentrated (54 %).

These three findings **complement, not contradict, QQ findings**:

- QQ's 2022 platform-split is about *which chart a song appears
  on*, not about *which artist dominates*.
- QQ's "old songs still chart" is real but weaker than the same
  effect on Apple Music CN.
- The QQ-vs-NetEase diversity gradient (24.5 % vs 9.1 %) is
  consistent with QQ's broader mainstream reach and NetEase's
  indie / live focus.

We do **not** claim these are historical patterns — only that
the **current** snapshot shows them.

## 9.3 What we did NOT attempt (and why)

Three follow-up questions would tighten the cross-platform
narrative but require additional data sources:

1. **Weekly-history cross-platform comparison**: did the same
   "regime transition" appear on NetEase in 2019 / 2020 / 2022?
   Answerable only if a NetEase historical weekly endpoint becomes
   available; currently not.
2. **Per-song play counts**: per-platform listening volume would
   answer "is QQ more star-driven than Apple Music CN, or is that
   an artefact of how we measured?". Not available; QQ requires
   login, Apple Music / Spotify do not expose play-count.
3. **Genre breakdown**: rap / pop / classical / folk share per
   platform. QQ's `genre_inferred` covers only rap / edm / guofeng.
   Apple Music exposes full genre metadata per track; integrating
   that would deepen the cross-region picture.

# 10. Limitations

1. **Coverage 2018-2024, not 2015-2025.** QQ's public API clamps the
   `period` parameter outside this window. We probe each year/week
   pair and keep only those honoured by the server.
2. **No audio features** (MERT / librosa / Jukemir / CLAP).
   Out-of-scope per user request. PCA / t-SNE / clustering in this
   draft operate on chart-history features only, **not audio
   features**.
3. **No song-level play counts / no lyrics / no song-detail fields**.
   All such endpoints now require login (code=500003). Genre is
   inferred from genre-tagged charts only.
4. **Cross-platform validation is structural, not historical.**
   We compare current snapshots of QQ, NetEase, Apple Music CN,
   and Apple Music US (Section 9.2). Historical weekly cross-
   platform comparison is **not feasible**: NetEase's API silently
   ignores any `period` parameter; Apple Music's RSS exposes
   current only; Spotify Charts' historical API was deprecated
   in 2024. Kugou, Douyin, Bilibili, and Last.fm all either lack
   public historical endpoints or require login. See
   `docs/CROSS_PLATFORM_NOTES.md` for the full feasibility matrix.
5. **Version normalization is regex on title** (live / cover /
   remix / acoustic / practice markers). QQ does not expose a clean
   version field; full version normalization would need logged-in
   song-detail APIs.
6. **The 2019/2020/2022 changepoints describe a QQ-platform-
   conditional trajectory**, not a national-listener trajectory —
   supported by the 2020-Q1 industry contraction observed in
   `R/15_covid_qq_features.R` and by Apple Music CN's much
   stronger "old catalogue" share (Section 9.2).

# 12. Reproducibility

```sh
# 0. Restore R environment (one-time)
Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'

# 1. Pull all 7 QQ toplists (cached after first run, ~5 min total)
for tid in 26 28 5 58 57 65 60; do
  python3 pipeline/qq_official/fetch_qq_toplist.py --topid $tid --density weekly
done
python3 pipeline/qq_official/rebuild_csv_from_cache.py \
  --topid 26 --topid 28 --topid 5 --topid 58 --topid 57 --topid 65 --topid 60

# 2. Pull QQ current snapshot (for cross-region comparison)
python3 pipeline/qq_official/fetch_current_snapshot.py

# 3. Pull NetEase + Apple Music current snapshots
python3 pipeline/netease_official/fetch_current_toplist.py
python3 pipeline/apple_music_official/fetch_current_charts.py --region cn --region us

# 4. R analysis (full pipeline, ~3 min)
Rscript R/01_clean.R
Rscript R/02_yearly_summary.R
Rscript R/03_umap.R
Rscript R/04_special_songs.R
Rscript R/05_changepoint.R
Rscript R/06_toplist_compare.R
Rscript R/07_version_normalize.R
Rscript R/08_topid_overview.R
Rscript R/09_genre_drift.R
Rscript R/14_lof_outliers.R
Rscript R/15_covid_qq_features.R
Rscript R/17_cross_region_patterns.R

# 5. knit report
PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("R/report.Rmd")'
```
